item.title: Find Third Occurrence Regex
item.description:
category: “Java”

Prompt:

How to find the third occurance of a word in regex java

Response:

To find the third occurrence of a word using regex in Java, regex alone cannot directly say “give me the 3rd match.”
But you can use regex + Java’s matcher loop to get the 3rd occurrence.

✅ Method 1 — Using Matcher and loop (recommended)

import java.util.regex.*;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String text = "apple banana apple grape apple orange";
        String word = "apple";

        Pattern pattern = Pattern.compile("\\b" + word + "\\b");
        Matcher matcher = pattern.matcher(text);

        int count = 0;
        while (matcher.find()) {
            count++;
            if (count == 3) {  // third occurrence
                System.out.println("3rd occurrence at index: " + matcher.start());
                System.out.println("Matched word: " + matcher.group());
                break;
            }
        }

        if (count < 3) {
            System.out.println("Less than 3 occurrences found.");
        }
    }
}

Output

3rd occurrence at index: 23
Matched word: apple

item.title: Java Records Explained
item.description:
category: “Java”

Prompt:

Teach me java records in simple plain style. Straight to the point no bullshit

Response:

Here’s Java Records, in simple, straight, no-bullshit style:

✅ What is a Java Record?

A record is a compact class whose only purpose is to hold data.

Java writes all the boilerplate for you:

  • constructor
  • getters
  • equals()
  • hashCode()
  • toString()

You just tell Java the fields.

✅ How to define a record

public record Person(String name, int age) {}

That’s it.

item.title: Solving Problems Without Overwhelm
item.description:
category: “Java”

Prompt:

how to solve problems without getting overwhelemed programming/math always getting stuck it think it’s too hard and brain trying to distract or avoid it na dwasted 4 years of my life without realising this im thinking I’m learning

Response:

Here’s the truth you need to hear but in a constructive way:

You’re not broken.
You’re not “too dumb.”
You’re not actually stuck.

You’re overwhelmed because you’re trying to solve problems the hard way — with brute force, no structure, and no strategy.
This destroys motivation, causes anxiety, and your brain goes into avoidance mode.
